newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power seen higher on San Onofre 3 nuke delay.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power seen higher on San Onofre 3 nuke delay.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were seen opening higher Friday on news that restart of unit 3 at the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station in southern California was delayed to Sunday night, market sources said.
Forecasts of continued triple-digit temperatures in parts of the Southwest are also expected to propel the power complex higher, brokers and traders said.
"People are going to focus on the generation and the heat," one Houston futures trader said.

In over-the-counter(OTC) business, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were talked at $36.80-37.10 a megawatt hour (MWh) after settling up two dollars yesterday at $36.68. August OTC PV was close to breaking its life-of-contract high at $37.30.
August OTC California-Oregon Border (COB) was quoted at $22.10-22.40 a MWh, firmer than yesterday's close at $22.04.
The 1,080 megawatt (MW) SONGS unit 3 remained off line, while engineers have been correcting a water contamination problem in the unit's lube oil system, the operator said.
The unit, in San Clemente, Calif., was scheduled earlier to return to service yesterday.
The adjacent 1,070 MW unit 2 was still holding at 70 percent power while maintenance work on a main feedwater pump is being carried out.
Market sources said weaker physical prices in the West will likely put a lid on a rise in futures prices.
"That should put a damper on things," another Houston futures trader said.
Firm, peak prices at PV for Monday fell to $45.00-46.00 a MWh from Thursday's $49.00-52.00 for today despite SONGS unit 3's delayed restart.
In other generation news, output at the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Richland, Washington, rose to 92 percent output early Friday.
The 750 MW Mohave coal-fired unit 3, which was shut Monday for repairs, was planned to resume operations Saturday.
The 254 MW Valmy coal-fired unit 1 in Nevada was unlikely to return to full power until the weekend, after its output was halved Tuesday because of a tube leak.
Separately, southbound capacity on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie transmission system was set to be cut by 250 MW to 3,200 MW again today between 0900 and 1600 PDT for maintenance work.
